data.topic: Auto-detection, self-learning, and auto-memory systems for AI coding agents — conflict detection in parallel multi-agent systems, self-learning memory architectures, autonomous coordination patterns, trust calibration and graduated autonomy
data.what: Integrate parallel coordination, self-learning, and graduated autonomy patterns from other AI agent systems into our dotclaude orchestration pipeline
data.audience: Kelsi (sole operator of the dotclaude system)
data.platform: CLI — Claude Code skills/hooks/MCP orchestration layer
in_scope: Conflict detection and prediction in multi-agent parallel coding systems
Self-learning memory architectures (correction pipelines, behavioral preference distillation, outcome-based learning)
Autonomous coordination patterns (merge queues, dependency graphs, write-target analysis)
Trust calibration and graduated autonomy (measurable gates for increasing agent independence)
Agent health monitoring and watchdog patterns
Auto-review and testing loops (Ralph Loop pattern)
Comparison with: Gastown/Beads, Devin, SWE-Agent, OpenHands, Cursor, Windsurf, Aider, Ralph Loop, academic research
out_of_scope: Building a separate Go/Rust binary (stay within Claude Code primitives)
Replicating GT's 20-30 agent scale for its own sake (scale follows need)
Replacing our existing memory system (extend it, don't rebuild)
Cost optimization as a primary goal (correctness and throughput first)
data.problem: Epic-level serialization limits throughput. Stories run in parallel but epics never do. Sequential merging is the actual ceiling. No agent health monitoring. No auto-review loops. Conflict detection is untested at scale.
data.why: Without cross-epic parallelism and a smart merge queue, we can't scale beyond 3-5 concurrent stories. The system works but doesn't compound its efficiency gains as project complexity grows.
data.end_goal: Research briefing that feeds directly into /ship — build changes to ORCHESTRATION.md, run-stories, merge-worktree, and new skills for agent health, merge queue, and graduated autonomy
data.complexity_reasoning: Requires surveying 10+ external systems and academic approaches across 4 research dimensions, then synthesizing into actionable changes to our orchestration layer
